utterances.text: I think, Your Honour -- I'm afraid -- for some reason I can't get into e-trans where I'm sitting. But it was what Mr. Krgovic -- what Mr. Aleksic suggested and I rather thought Your Honours may have agreed with it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: No, my recollection is --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: What you are now articulating is what we in fact said.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, it was argued at the time -- Mr. Aleksic certainly said there should have been a motion filed and we utterly disagree with that, but, Your Honours, I'm sorry, I obviously misunderstood Your Honour's ruling in which case I wasted my time on that and I'm sorry about that. Your Honours, the second matter relates to this morning and this question of the proofing notes. Your Honours, what, as Mr. Olmsted pointed out, came out of a five-day proofing with this witness, as we now learnt for the first time is a considerable amount of extra evidence. And as we've said before, we're hampered by the fact that we have no statements, occasionally an interview. On this occasion, as Your Honours heard from the witness, some short chats which were not specifically helpful and certainly, as Mr. Olmsted pointed out, didn't deal with any of the topics. Your Honours, as it so happens, we got the proofing note at just after 9.00 on Friday night and we do say, given how long this witness was here, that was far too late. Of course Mr. Olmsted is prepared to work over the weekend, but we don't want to ask administrative staff to come in over the weekend to prepare extra documents as a result of extra information which could have been ascertained months and months ago and we should have been provided with proper amended 65 ter summaries. Your Honours, the 65 ter summaries for upcoming witnesses are just as bad. They are vague in the extreme, they give the Prosecution absolutely only the -- a surface indication of what the witness is going to talk about. Your Honours, therefore, given there's now going to be a further two-week break, first of all, Your Honour, we would ask for confirmation by Wednesday of which witness is actually coming after the break. I understand from Mr. Krgovic there may be difficulties with the order as it presently is. And so if there's to be a change, we would like to know about it. Secondly, that the -- a proper proofing note is supplied to us with details of what the witness is actually going to talk about 72 hours in advance of the witness coming into the witness box. Your Honours, we don't think that's an unreasonable request. As I say, we have no statements, nothing for most of these witnesses. So, Your Honours, that's the situation as -- in respect we would ask for proper notification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Aleksic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will be brief, Your Honour. My colleague, Mr. Olmsted, had occasion to respond to my objection and of course he did say what he had to say, and I do appreciate that Mrs. Korner is entitled to come and further expand on the position of their party. But I would also appreciate it, since Mr. Zecevic and Krgovic are not present today, to be allowed to address the Trial Chamber tomorrow morning in relation to the first item. As for the second matter --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Well, I thought that matter was -- I don't think we need to hear counsel further on that. And as regards the -- I don't know what your response is going to be the second item, but the frustration that Ms. Korner has indicated in terms of inadequacy of a proofing note is clearly understood and everybody's going to agree that there ought to be proper proofing notes. But the question that I would ask you to address, either now or first thing tomorrow morning, is that once we get past the motherhood and apple pie stage, in other words, the point at which we all agree, how do you propose practically to address this concern?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I would like to consult Mr. Krgovic on this issue, and if that is suitable I would like to address the Trial Chamber tomorrow morning if that's acceptable. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... Practical solution. Yes, so we rise to resume tomorrow morning at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 18th day of October, 2011, at 9.00 a.m.
